## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.  
Back up user rows before merge because migration 3 permanently drops legacy email values from the live table. Order recovery also needs to handle the schema change before replacing live rows.

## Changes
The pull request adds SQLite migrations that drop `users.legacy_email` and `orders.coupon_code`. It adds a test that checks both columns are removed and the orders backup retains the original coupon code.

## Critical
- migrations/m0003_drop_legacy_email.py:7 — correctness — Back up users before dropping legacy email — A user whose legacy email was set after migration 2 loses that value when migration 3 drops the column without calling `backup_table`. The version 2 snapshot predates the update. — Operators cannot recover those legacy email values from the migration backups. — Fix: Follow the backup pattern in `migrations/m0002_drop_nickname.py:7` and extend `test_drop_retired_columns`.

## Important
- migrations/m0004_drop_coupon_code.py:8 — correctness — Restore the orders schema before replacing rows — After migration 4 drops `coupon_code`, `restore_table(conn, "orders", 4)` deletes the live orders, then fails at `migrations/safety.py:15` because the backup has four columns and the live table has three. — On an autocommit connection, a recovery attempt leaves the live orders table empty. — Fix: Restore the missing column before copying rows and make the replacement in `migrations/safety.py:13` atomic.
